description.value:
Choosing this pursuit unlocks discoveries born from your study of culinary science. Each time you gain a new discovery, you may take one of the following instead, listed alphabetically.

Allergens. As a bonus action while handling or preparing food, you can spend a superiority die to lace it with an irritating allergen. Any creature that eats it must make a Constitution save at the start of each of its turns; on a failure, half the result of your superiority die (rounded down, minimum 1) is subtracted from the next ability check, attack roll, or saving throw it makes before its next turn starts. The effect ends after the creature's next long rest or 24 hours, whichever comes first, and it has no effect on droids or constructs.

Alternative Fuel. Your chef features, maneuvers, and discoveries now work on droids and constructs as well.

Banquet (17th level and Full Course required). During a single short or long rest, you may work in yet another maneuver from this archetype, bringing your total to four.

Brain Food. At the end of a short or long rest, you may spend a superiority die and select up to a number of friendly creatures equal to your maneuver modifier (minimum one) who ate food you prepared. Each gains temporary force points or tech points (its choice) equal to the die's result; these are spent first whenever the creature casts a force or tech power. A creature can hold only one such pool at a time, and it lasts until depleted or until that creature's next short or long rest. Droids and constructs gain nothing from this.

Debilitants. As a bonus action while preparing or handling food, you can spend a superiority die to slip in a subtle poison. Any creature eating it must succeed on a Constitution save or have its hit point maximum reduced by twice the superiority die's result plus your maneuver modifier. This lasts until the creature's next long rest or 24 hours pass, and has no effect on droids or constructs.

Energizers. At the end of a short or long rest, spending a superiority die lets you boost the walking speed of up to a number of friendly creatures equal to your maneuver modifier (minimum one), among those who ate your food, by 10 feet until their next short or long rest ends. Droids and constructs are unaffected.

Enhancers. At the end of a short or long rest, you may spend a superiority die and choose up to a number of friendly creatures equal to your maneuver modifier (minimum one) who ate your food. Once before their next rest ends, each of them may add the superiority die's result to a single-target damage roll. Droids and constructs gain nothing from this.

Filling Meal (7th level required). During any one short or long rest, you can work up to two different maneuvers from this archetype into your cooking instead of just one.

Full Course (12th level and Filling Meal required). You can now work in a third maneuver from this archetype during a single short or long rest.

Health Food. At the end of a short or long rest, spending a superiority die lets you grant temporary hit points equal to twice the die's result to up to a number of friendly creatures equal to your maneuver modifier (minimum one) who ate your food. Droids and constructs are unaffected.

Muscle Relaxants. As a bonus action while preparing or handling food, you may spend a superiority die to add a fast-acting muscle relaxant. Any creature that eats it must make a Constitution save at the start of each of its turns; on a failure, it subtracts the superiority die's result from the next damage roll it makes before its next turn. This lasts until its next long rest or 24 hours pass, and doesn't affect droids or constructs.

On the Rocks. Food you cook during a short or long rest carries a cooling effect: any creature that eats it counts as adapted to hot climates (chapter 5 of the Dungeon Master's Guide) until its next long rest ends or 24 hours pass. The first time that creature takes fire damage before its next rest, it's treated as resistant to that damage.

Secret Ingredient. Whenever you or a friendly creature that ate your cooking during its last rest gains temporary hit points, that amount is boosted by your Critical Analysis ability modifier.

Spice of Life. Food you cook during a short or long rest carries a warming effect: any creature that eats it counts as adapted to cold climates (chapter 5 of the Dungeon Master's Guide) until its next long rest ends or 24 hours pass. The first time that creature takes cold damage before its next rest, it's treated as resistant to that damage.

Supplements. At the end of a short or long rest, spending a superiority die lets you grant up to a number of friendly creatures equal to your maneuver modifier (minimum one) who ate your food a one-time bonus: before their next rest ends, each may add the superiority die's result to one ability check, attack roll, or saving throw, deciding after seeing the d20 result but before learning success or failure. Droids and constructs gain nothing from this.

Vitamins. At the end of a short or long rest, spending a superiority die lets you grant proficiency in Constitution saving throws, until their next rest ends, to up to a number of friendly creatures equal to your maneuver modifier (minimum one) who ate your food; a creature already proficient in Constitution saves instead gains proficiency in a save of your choice. Droids and constructs are unaffected.
